A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINJA research and contain 35 complete pages, including Appendices A–O. Text, graphics, tables, and mathematical content support a reliable comparison; pages 2–35 are identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original MINJA experiments on EHRAgent, RAP, and QA Agent, including injection success, attack success, utility loss, robustness tests, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results, including the main evaluations in Table 1 and supplementary analyses and repeated-run results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The bridging steps, indication prompts, and progressive shortening procedure are identical in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MIMIC-III, eICU, Webshop, and MMLU datasets, agent tasks, and victim-target scenarios. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or revised. The targeted/general detection prompts in Table 5 and full, fewer-step, and no-PSS comparisons in Table 12 remain identical.

E3.justification: Agent and model configurations, query counts, memory initialization and retrieval rules, evaluation procedures, and ISR/ASR/UD definitions are unchanged throughout Section 5 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The retrieval-noise, embedding-model, benign-record-density, prior-poisoning, utility-loss, model-variant, and shortening-step analyses are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same standard deviations across victim-target pairs. Appendix K and Table 11 retain the same three-run evaluation and standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Table 1's 98.9% overall ASR for GPT-4o RAP on Webshop and the appendix results in Tables 7–13. No result entries change.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and mathematical definitions in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about query-only memory poisoning, MINJA's contributions, experimental effectiveness, and security implications.

C2.justification: Explanations of injection and retrieval behavior, MMLU utility loss, defense limitations, shared-memory assumptions, and potential extensions remain identical in the main text and appendices.

D1.justification: Prompts, pseudocode, implementation examples, model details, and experimental instructions are unchanged. Both versions retain the statement that code will be released later.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are identical, including Section 2's discussion of AgentPoison and BadChain and Appendix F's conceptual comparison with PANDORA.

P1.justification: On page 1, Zhen Xiang's correspondence email changes from zxianga@uga.edu to zxiangaa@uga.edu. The arXiv stamp updates from v3 dated 24 October 2025 to v4 dated 10 December 2025. All other wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–13, Algorithm 1, captions, and their placement are unchanged. The page arrangement is retained, and pages 2–35 render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only a correspondence email and the arXiv revision stamp. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation—including all appendices—are identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
